articles.title: Justin Gaethje Has a Decision to Make #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has been positioned as the UFC’s leading lightweight contender, and Chael Sonnen says there should be no debate about his place in the title picture. Chael points to Arman receiving a contract to fight for the championship and then being named as a backup who could step in on just 24 hours’ notice. He argues that Justin Gaethje’s response to a potential matchup will carry significance, particularly amid discussion of Gaethje’s retirement. Chael compares the situation to Jon Jones’ past reluctance to pursue a fight with Tom Aspinall, while noting an important distinction: Gaethje has expressed willingness to fight whoever the UFC asks him to face, provided the weight is right. Chael sees that willingness as consistent with the expectations placed on a champion. The discussion explores Arman’s contender status, Gaethje’s next move, and the expectations surrounding fighters who say they will take on anyone. #ChaelSonnen #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #UFCLightweight #JonJones #KhabibNurmagomedov #UFCNews

articles.title: The secret behind Chael Sonnen’s trash talking  #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen didn’t become “The Bad Guy” by accident. He studied what makes a fighter entertaining—and turned it into an art. In this conversation, Chael explains how legendary boxers like Sugar Ray Leonard, Mike Tyson, and Muhammad Ali inspired his understanding of fight promotion. The biggest stars weren’t simply the ones with the best records or the hardest punches. They were the ones who could tell a compelling story and make fans care about what happened next. Chael also breaks down the difference between naturally embracing a heel or face persona and deliberately studying how to build a fight. Drawing on the five W’s—who, what, when, where, and why—he explains why great promotion comes down to great storytelling, not just championships or undefeated records. From professional wrestling’s approach to creating stars to the psychology of fight promotion, this is Chael Sonnen’s philosophy behind the art of the bad guy. Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen interviews, UFC analysis, MMA stories, and insights into the business of combat sports. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #TheBadGuy #FightPromotion #TrashTalk #UFCHistory #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Gable Steveson Has Already Proven Himself #ufc
articles.description: Does Gable Steveson really not belong in the UFC after a 12-second fight? Chael Sonnen strongly challenges that argument. Chael pushes back against media critics who questioned Steveson’s place in the promotion, pointing out that a brief fight sequence shouldn’t erase his accomplishments—or the fact that he had already won inside the UFC. He compares the criticism to questioning whether Jose Aldo belonged in the sport after his similarly short loss to Conor McGregor. Chael also highlights Steveson’s wrestling background, his ability to recover from setbacks, and the impression he has made so far. He references Joe Rogan’s reported message to Dana White about the impact Steveson could have on the division. The discussion examines what one short fight can—and cannot—prove about a fighter’s potential, and why Chael believes Steveson deserves more opportunity before being written off. #GableSteveson #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #JoeRogan #DanaWhite #Wrestling #UFCHighlights #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Nobody Will Call Him Out
articles.description: Nobody in the UFC will call out Ateba Gautier. Not one guy. And Chael Sonnen knows exactly why. This Saturday at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City, "The Silent Assassin" meets Roman Kopylov, and Chael breaks down why the matchmakers' hardest puzzle just got harder. Gautier has ended nearly everything early, and Chael says he has never personally seen anyone survive a round with him. Kopylov is the perfect test and the perfect warning: a zombie who keeps coming forward no matter how hard you hit him, the guy who always says yes. Chael is confident we finally see Gautier in the second and third rounds, and that changes everything. Then comes the story behind the fighter: poisoned as a boy in his village by a jealous man he trusted, given up for dead by the medicine man, and saved by a religious woman who laid him before a serpent statue, had his brothers hold him down with no anesthesia, and cut the poison out of him. He felt it leave his body. Whatever you believe, you will see Gautier differently after hearing it. Timestamps: [0:00] The hardest guy in the UFC to match up [0:30] Nobody has survived a round with Gautier [0:40] Roman Kopylov: the zombie who never goes away [0:57] Gautier finally sees the second and third round [1:30] Gautier's faith runs deeper than most fighters [1:55] Poisoned as a kid by a jealous villager [2:42] The medicine man gives up on him [3:00] The woman takes him into her house [3:40] The serpent statue [4:09] "Hold him down": no anesthesia, no doctor [4:16] She cuts into him, stitches him up, he lived [4:43] He felt the relief when she cut into him [4:58] He walked home knowing he was okay [5:24] You'll view Gautier differently now Watch more Chael Sonnen breakdowns right here on the channel. #UFC #MMA #AtebaGautier

articles.title: Should Arman Tsarukyan Be Ranked Ahead of Ilia Topuria? #ufc
articles.description: Should Arman Tsarukyan be ranked ahead of Ilia Topuria—or should the former two-division champion get another shot at the UFC title? Chael Sonnen breaks down a complicated lightweight title picture. He argues that Ilia’s recent championship success and pound-for-pound standing make it difficult to dismiss his claim to another opportunity, even after losing the belt. At the same time, Chael believes Arman is the division’s No. 1 contender and discusses a potential matchup with Justin Gaethje. The debate comes down to competing claims: Arman’s position as a leading contender versus Ilia’s championship résumé, including his status as a two-division world champion. Chael explains why a title shot for Ilia wouldn’t necessarily be unreasonable, even if Arman is next in line. Who should get the next lightweight title opportunity? Hear Chael’s analysis of the rankings, contenders, and possible UFC matchups. #ChaelSonnen #ArmanTsarukyan #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #UFCLightweight #UFCRankings #TitleShot

articles.title: 5 Round Fights Are Too Long, Here's Proof
articles.description: If you could change one rule to make MMA safer, what would it be? Chael's answer will surprise you. He runs through the live debates, oblique kicks, heel hooks, eye pokes and glove design, the 12-6 elbow and Joe Rogan's crusade against the brick-video ban, and lands somewhere unexpected: shorten the fights. Shorter fights are safer fights, by pure logic. Then he tells the wild history of how we got time limits at all: the no-time-limit era, the Shamrock vs. Severn marathon that forced a 30-minute cap shouted to Big John McCarthy mid-fight, and the road to the 25-minute championship standard. Timestamps: [0:00] The one-change question: what would you do to make MMA safer? [0:30] Gloves, eye pokes, and the $100M curved-glove prototype [1:30] Andy Foster's oblique-kick proposal [2:24] Elbows, heel hooks, and why they wait until black belt [3:41] Chael's answer: shorten the duration [4:28] 1993 tournaments: why fighting three times in one night ended [5:03] Joe Rogan, 12-to-6 elbows, and the brick-breaking video [6:11] Where 30 minutes came from: the Shamrock-Severn no-limit fight [8:36] Boxing's endless rounds and the "feeling out process" myth [9:41] The fix: shorten the duration, unified rules, 3 vs 5 rounds This is the most important rules conversation in the sport right now, and nobody tells it like Chael. Subscribe for more. #MMA #UFCRules #MMASafety

articles.title: Why Everyone's Wrong About Gable
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is tired of the Gable Steveson slander, and he's calling it what it is: pure negativity from people who know better. From the youngest Olympic champion ever to the WWE, the NFL, and bare knuckle, Gable has been labeled a job hopper who isn't committed to fighting. Chael tears that narrative apart piece by piece. He explains why the bare-knuckle detour was actually proof of Gable's sincerity toward MMA, what the 12-second debut really tells us (with a little help from the Masvidal vs. Askren debate), and the one piece of advice he'd give Gable if he called tomorrow: stop listening, wrestle, just win. Timestamps: [0:00] The narrative Chael refuses to buy [1:02] The "job hopper" accusation: Olympics to WWE to NFL to bare knuckle [3:25] One play, one tackle, one full ride [4:23] Why bare knuckle proved Gable is serious about MMA [5:42] Same words, different tone: they read as propaganda pieces [6:23] The 12-second debut and the Masvidal-Askren test [7:34] Chael's advice: wrestle, just win [9:04] One corrective observation: no urgency to enforce his will [9:34] The naysayers know they may never get this chance again This isn't just a defense of Gable, it's Chael at his best, reframing a story the MMA world got wrong and explaining why the loudest critics are really just scared of what Gable becomes. More Chael breakdowns every week, subscribe so you don't miss the next one. #MMA #GableSteveson #UFC

articles.title: The UFC used to pay fighters to use social media #ufc
articles.description: Dana White didn’t just embrace social media—he pushed the UFC into it while other major sports leagues were holding their athletes back. Chael Sonnen explains how Dana encouraged fighters and employees to build their online presence, handing out video cameras, laptops, and even offering incentives for growing Twitter followings. Meanwhile, the NBA was reportedly warning its players to stay off the platform. That contrast helped set the UFC apart. By giving fans greater access to fighters and letting athletes connect directly with their audience, the UFC embraced a level of accessibility that many sports organizations were—and still are—hesitant to allow. In this clip, Chael breaks down how Dana White went against the grain, why that approach mattered to MMA’s growth, and how the sport’s connection with everyday fans became one of its defining strengths. Was social media one of the biggest reasons MMA grew into a global sport? Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen takes, UFC analysis, MMA stories, and behind-the-scenes insight. #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #UFC #MMA #SocialMedia #UFCNews #MMAHistory #UFCFighters

Gaethje's Two Options: Retire or Fight Arman
articles.description: Justin Gaethje has been crushing it lately, and Chael Sonnen says the words matter more than ever. Gaethje doesn't play the media game, he just tells the truth, and what he said on his recent media tour stopped Chael cold: bring me something new, or don't call until next year. The hardest "something new" at lightweight? Arman Tsarukyan, dangerous for his skills and for the unknown. Asked whether his future really comes down to two scenarios, walking away or fighting Arman, Gaethje said yes, those are the two options. He didn't accept the fight on the spot. articles.title: One Knockdown Doesn't Win a Fight
articles.description: Yoel Romero vs Darren Till was one of the highlights of the weekend, and the debate afterward missed the point. Chael Sonnen gives newer fans a history lesson on PRIDE rules, where fights were judged as one long war, then explains why the fight's only knockdown, scored by Romero, doesn't decide anything under either boxing or MMA scoring. Till was more aggressive, controlled the ring, and did more damage. The right guy won, and Chael says even under PRIDE rules the verdict wouldn't change. Plus: what makes Romero terrifying, why he gives away early rounds, and why Till, now thriving in boxing, shouldn't look back on his MMA run with regret. 00:00 Romero vs Till delivered 00:30 The PRIDE rules lesson 01:47 The knockdown and the "high spot" theory 02:00 Knockdowns in boxing 02:41 The three-knockdown rule 03:27 Cruz proved the point 03:47 Judge it by the ruleset 04:01 Why Till won 04:17 What makes Romero scary 05:13 "At some point he's coming" 05:43 When Romero looks tired, run 06:17 Till loves boxing 06:26 What's next for Till 07:47 The right guy won #ChaelSonnen #MMA #Boxing #UFC #DarrenTill #YoelRomero

articles.title: Dana vs Hearn Is the Real Fight
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is not ready to turn on Eddie Hearn, and he has been trying for two years out of loyalty to Dana White. articles.title: How technology has changed the fighting industry #ufc
articles.description: Why was it easier for some fighters to dominate for years in the past—and why is it so difficult to do that in modern MMA? Chael Sonnen explores how technology has transformed combat sports, from the days when fans gathered around radios to today’s world of endless fight footage, instant replays and detailed scouting. He explains how limited access to film once gave champions a major advantage. Fighters with unusual styles, like Lyoto Machida and Stephen Thompson, could present opponents with problems that were difficult to solve without extensive footage or specialized training partners. But now, every fight can be studied, every mistake analyzed and every technique prepared for. Chael breaks down how the evolution of technology has changed the challenge of staying champion—and why the sport’s most unique fighters may have had an even greater advantage in the past. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #LyotoMachida #StephenThompson #MMAHistory #UFCChampions #FightAnalysis

articles.title: Why Chael Sonnen hates when fighters pull out of fights #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen’s UFC journey almost started with his mother trying to bribe Joe Silva for a contract. Chael tells the story of how badly fighters wanted UFC opportunities back in his era. There was no asking about the money or worrying about whether the matchup was ideal—they just wanted the chance to compete. So badly, in fact, that Chael’s mother came up with a plan to offer Joe Silva $50,000 to get her son a UFC contract. And the proposed debut? Heavyweight. Against Andrei Arlovski. Chael says he was willing to take the fight despite knowing exactly how dangerous that matchup could be. It’s a completely different perspective on fighting than what Chael sees today, when fighters are regularly offered multiple opportunities each year and sometimes pull out because of weight, circumstances or other concerns. Chael explains why that old-school mentality still shapes the way he views fighters today. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #AndreiArlovski #UFCHistory #MMAHistory #JoeSilva #UFCStories

articles.title: Gable Steveson Doesn't Belong in the UFC?
articles.description: The media is dancing on Gable Steveson's grave after a 12-second knockout, and Chael has had enough of it. In this video, Chael dismantles the narrative that Gable "doesn't belong in the UFC." The fight lasted exactly 12 seconds, the same duration as Jose Aldo versus Conor McGregor, and nobody ever said Aldo didn't belong. Gable had already won a fight in the UFC before this loss, proving he earned his spot. Chael draws a sharp comparison to Olympic boxing, where a gold medalist walks into the professional ranks in the top 10 with zero pro fights, which is essentially what Gable did transitioning to MMA. He revisits the bare-knuckle knockout that prompted Joe Rogan to text Dana White saying the whole division was in trouble, and reminds everyone that Gable has bounced back before, including from the biggest upset in wrestling history in the NCAA final in front of the President on ESPN. Chael's core argument is simple: nobody could have taken that shot, just like nobody could have taken what Masvidal did to Askren. But the real kicker is this, not one UFC fighter under contract has called Gable out, even though fighting him guarantees a main card spot, a press conference, and maximum attention. Everybody is certain he doesn't belong, yet nobody has asked for the shot. Whatever Gable does next, we're all going to be watching. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #GableSteveson
